claims.text: The modeled material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen in a near-BCC structure.
The oxygen impurities are randomly distributed in the initial material model.
Explicitly modeling oxygen impurity clusters with combined DFT and MD will improve conductivity predictions for oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr over both 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
The framework will insert oxygen clusters at an overall oxygen content of 1 wt.% and calibrate their configurations against experimental data.
Sensitivity analysis over oxygen-cluster configurations will be used to assess robustness.
The inserted oxygen clusters will reproduce experimentally observed defect densities.
Oxygen impurity clusters disrupt the periodic crystal potential and form localized defect states.
Oxygen-cluster defect states act as scattering centers for both electrons and phonons.
At low temperatures, oxygen clusters induce localized electronic states that increase electron scattering and lower conductivity relative to a defect-free crystal.
At high temperatures, thermal activation causes partial dissociation of oxygen defects.
At high temperatures, oxygen defects enhance phonon scattering and thereby moderate the increase in conductivity.
Different temperature regimes can exhibit different defect-related conduction mechanisms.
The simulated conductivity at 150 K will agree with experiment within ±5%.
The oxygen-containing material will have lower cryogenic conductivity than predicted for an ideal defect-free crystal.
Its high-temperature conductivity increase will be more moderate than that predicted by idealized models.
Existing analytical models assume perfect, defect-free crystals and consequently overestimate HfNbTaTiZr conductivity by neglecting oxygen-induced scattering.
The proposed model is limited to bulk HfNbTaTiZr near 1 wt.% oxygen and the temperature intervals 0–200 K and 300–1200 K unless recalibrated.
A deviation greater than 10% from the experimental conductivity at 150 K, or failure to reproduce the specified temperature trends, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state specifies a random distribution of oxygen impurities, whereas the intervention and mediator rely on explicitly clustered oxygen; the hypothesis does not define how the random and clustered descriptions are reconciled.
